title: Getting started
intro: Build an economy, scout your opponents, and lead an army through three ages. Start with a small map and one opponent while learning the controls.

panels.title: Your first match
steps: Choose Start Game, your faction, map size and opponents in Match Setup. Easy difficulty gives you more time to react.
Select a Worker and right-click a tree or gold deposit. Split workers across nearby nodes, and keep paths around buildings clear.
Build a Farm early: food is produced automatically. Train more Workers at the Town Center, but keep enough resources for your first Barracks.
Build Houses before the population bar fills. Train a small mixed army, scout nearby ground, and protect your workers before expanding.
Select the Town Center and open Upgrades when you are ready to advance to Bronze Age.

panels.title: Winning and rebuilding
paragraphs: Annihilation eliminates a player only when they have no Town Center, Town Hall or Castle, no foundation for one, and no surviving Workers, including sheltered Workers. Destroying the main building alone may not finish the opponent: a surviving Worker can rebuild.

Annihilation matches that remain unresolved end in a draw after 40 minutes of game time. Economic victory requires {economic_target} cumulative gathered resources; spending resources does not reduce that total. Timed victory compares scores after {timed_minutes} game minutes. Elimination still applies in those modes.

panels.title: Match options
paragraphs: Difficulty changes how often the AI makes strategic decisions and how readily it launches attacks. Easy, Normal and Hard work independently of faction and personality. Rusher, Boomer, Turtle and Balanced personalities favor different plans.

Spectate AI Battle lets you watch AI opponents with the map revealed to you; the AI still uses its own fog of war. Map size limits the number of opponents. The game supports up to eight players including AI seats.
Mutators can change the normal opening or victory conditions. Use None for the standard rules described in this manual. A map seed lets you revisit the same generated terrain.

title: Ages and upgrades
intro: Age research unlocks options and refreshes your settlement's appearance. Military unit lines require their own paid upgrades.

panels.title: Stone Age
paragraphs: Begin with Workers, Clubmen, Slingers and Wooden Spearmen. Your civic building is called the Town Center. Available economic buildings include Houses, Farms, Lumbermills and Mines, alongside the Barracks.

panels.title: Bronze Age
paragraphs: Complete three Stone Age buildings other than the Town Center. Houses, Farms, Barracks, Lumbermills and Mines count; duplicates count too. Select the Town Center, open Upgrades, and pay for Advance to Bronze Age.

Your Town Center becomes a Town Hall and existing buildings and Workers gain Bronze artwork. Stables, Temples, Watchtowers, Markets, Blacksmiths and Siege Workshops become available, subject to their building prerequisites. Cavalry, healers, Ballistas and your faction's special unit unlock.

panels.title: Iron Age
paragraphs: After Bronze Age, complete a Blacksmith and two different specialist buildings chosen from Stable, Temple, Watchtower, Market and Siege Workshop. Research Advance to Iron Age at your Town Hall.
Your civic building becomes a Castle. Existing buildings and Workers gain Iron artwork, and the final military-line upgrades become available.

panels.title: Train or upgrade?
paragraphs: Train recruits one new unit. An upgrade improves every existing and future unit in that line for your player. Advancing an age alone does not turn Clubmen into Swordsmen or Mounted Spearmen into Heavy Cavalry.

A building has separate Train and Upgrades tabs. Selecting a different building, or clearing and reselecting, returns to its default tab. Hover over a disabled option to see the missing age, building, technology, resources or population space.
Blacksmith research has six families with three levels each. Only the next available level is shown. Improvements stack with unit-line upgrades.

title: Factions
intro: Both factions share the core economy, buildings and seven common unit lines. Each adds one exclusive Bronze Age unit.

panels.title: Steppe Clans
paragraphs: Train Horse Archers at the Stable after reaching Bronze Age. Use their speed and ranged attacks to raid exposed workers, pressure Axemen and reposition. Spears, enemy cavalry and Watchtowers are dangerous counters.

panels.title: Highland Clans
paragraphs: Train Axemen at the Barracks after reaching Bronze Age. They deal strong damage to sword infantry but are vulnerable to Slingers, Archers and Horse Archers. Give them cover as they close the distance.

panels.title: Choosing opponents
paragraphs: Your faction and the AI faction are chosen separately in Match Setup. AI faction may also be Random. Faction determines the exclusive unit; personality determines the AI's priorities; difficulty changes decision cadence and attack readiness.

title: Economy and expansion
intro: Food sustains recruitment, wood builds your settlement, and gold funds troops and research. Watch income as well as your current stockpile.

panels.title: Food comes from Farms
paragraphs: A completed Farm produces {farm_amount} food every {farm_interval} game seconds ({farm_rate} food per second). No Worker needs to gather there. Most units cost food; Ballistas instead cost wood and gold.

Four Farms cover the base food cost of continuously training Workers at one Town Center. Military recruitment needs additional Farms. Build food income before opening several training queues at once. Faster game speed accelerates both production and consumption.

panels.title: Wood and gold
paragraphs: Right-click a tree or gold deposit with selected Workers. Workers carry resources to an appropriate drop-off and then return. Lumbermills accept wood, Mines accept gold, and your civic building can accept both.

Before upgrades, a Worker gathers up to {wood_rate} wood or {gold_rate} gold per game second while actively working. Walking, drop-off travel and congestion reduce delivered income. Place drop-offs close to resources with room to approach.

Up to {node_capacity} workers can gather from one node at full rate. Spread larger groups across neighboring trees or deposits. Workers look for nearby resources as nodes run out and retry temporary interruptions; press F1 to find anyone who still needs an order.

panels.title: Population and queues
paragraphs: Your base capacity is {base_population}; each completed House adds {house_population}. Living units and paid training orders use population space. A full queue can therefore prevent another building from recruiting even before those units appear.

A training queue lists each unit type separately. The building's progress bar shows the current recruit; later entries wait their turn. Cancelling active production refunds half its cost; cancelling a paid queued recruit refunds its cost.

panels.title: Markets and investment
paragraphs: At a Market, sell {market_lot} wood or food for {market_sell} gold, or spend {market_buy} gold to buy {market_lot}. Trade has a cost, so use it to cover a shortfall while fixing your income.

Reserve resources for age advancement and research, but do not stop making Farms, Houses and defenses when your settlement needs them. Upgrade prices and effects are listed in the technology tables below.

title: Combat and worker safety
intro: Mixed armies are stronger than a single unit type. Protect your support units, scout before attacking, and keep a route home.

panels.title: Build a supporting army
bullets: Sword infantry forms the front line. Spearmen protect against cavalry. Ranged units need space and protection while they fire.
Mounted Spearmen and Heavy Cavalry are mobile raiders. Use them against exposed ranged units and workers; avoid running into spears or concentrated tower fire.

Ballistas have high ranged siege damage but only {ballista_hp} base HP and no base armor. Keep infantry between them and enemy melee troops. Upgrading to Heavy Ballista improves damage and range, not durability.

Healers automatically restore {heal_amount} HP every {heal_interval} game second to the most-wounded ally within {heal_range} world units. Keep them just behind the fighting line and move them along with the army. Priest research adds armor.
Neutral Healing Fountains heal nearby units from either side. Secure the area before resting a wounded army there.

panels.title: Commands, stances and formations
paragraphs: Right-click an enemy to focus it. Use Attack Move from the command card to advance while engaging enemies along the route. Shift queues supported orders so units can carry out a sequence.

Aggressive pursues nearby enemies. Defensive fights within a limited area. Stand Ground stays in place and attacks targets in range. No Attack is useful for retreating or scouting. Cycle stances with S and formations with F, or use the command card.

panels.title: Workers take shelter
paragraphs: Threatened Workers automatically try to shelter in a friendly Town Center, Town Hall, Castle or Watchtower. Shelter has limited capacity; workers without a free place try to retreat. Carried resources and the previous job are preserved.

After six safe game seconds, sheltered Workers return to their previous tasks. Manual garrison orders are also available for Workers. Use the building's Ungarrison command to release them. Military troops cannot garrison.

panels.title: Warnings and fog of war
paragraphs: Attacks on your forces trigger a spoken warning and flashing rings on the minimap. Click the minimap to inspect the area. L opens the event log, and Home returns to your main base.
Idle-worker alerts wait four seconds before notifying you and are rate limited. Use the idle-worker badge or F1 to find workers needing orders.

Explored terrain remains visible under fog, but current enemy activity requires vision. Combat sounds are suppressed in unexplored and fog-covered areas even if your camera is there. Visible sound effects are also limited by camera distance.

title: Controls and saving
intro: These are the default bindings. Change supported hotkeys in Settings. The command card shows its current shortcuts.

panels.title: Selection and camera
bullets: Left-click selects an object. Drag a box to select a group; Shift adds to the selection.
Right-click issues a context-sensitive order: move, gather, attack, build, repair or worker garrison. Shift + right-click queues supported orders.
WASD, arrow keys and edge scrolling pan the camera. The mouse wheel zooms. Click the minimap to move the view.
Ctrl + 1–9 assigns a control group; 1–9 recalls it. Command-card keys are Q, E, R, T on the top row and Z, X, C, V on the bottom row.
Right-click ground with a production building selected to set its rally point. A resource rally sends newly trained Workers toward that resource.
Select a foundation to cancel construction for a half refund. Hold Demolish on a completed building to remove it without a refund.

panels.title: Save, pause and resume
paragraphs: Esc opens the pause menu. Save and Load use the visible slots; F5 quick-saves to slot 0 and F9 loads it. You can also load from the main menu. Delete a save only if you intend to lose it: deletion requires a second confirmation.

Saves preserve the map, units, economy, ages, upgrades, queues, fog and worker jobs. Immediate combat targets and paths are reconstructed after loading, so units may briefly reconsider their movement.

Installed and portable Windows builds keep saves and settings in %LOCALAPPDATA%\RTS. Updating or uninstalling the game keeps those files. Source runs keep local user files in the source folder. Older saves are migrated when loaded.
The Help button in the main menu or pause menu opens this manual in your default browser. It works offline and does not require a login.

title: Troubleshooting
intro: The game is a playable beta. Reports with a save and clear steps help reproduce remaining problems.

panels.title: I keep running out of food
paragraphs: Build more Farms and slow recruitment until income catches up. Farms work automatically; assigning Workers to them does not increase output. Several active military buildings can consume food much faster than a single Town Center.

panels.title: A unit or upgrade is unavailable
paragraphs: Hover over the command to read its requirement. Check your age, faction, completed prerequisite buildings, earlier line upgrades, resources and population. Bronze Age unlocks special units, but only Steppe can train Horse Archers and only Highland can train Axemen.

panels.title: A Worker has stopped gathering
paragraphs: First check whether it is carrying cargo, returning to a drop-off, sheltering, or retrying a blocked approach. These are active tasks. If it remains idle, use F1 and right-click a reachable tree or deposit. Spread crowded workers out and leave approaches to drop-off buildings open.

panels.title: The game is slow or a match will not end
paragraphs: Lower the resolution, reduce game speed, or choose a smaller map and fewer opponents. Large late-game armies and tight passages remain areas of active improvement.

Look for surviving enemy Workers, a civic building foundation, or sheltered Workers after destroying the main base. They can keep an opponent alive. Unresolved Annihilation matches draw at 40 minutes of game time.

panels.title: Download and launch
paragraphs: For the portable version, extract the entire ZIP and run RTS/RTS.exe; do not move the executable away from its _internal folder. The installer creates a Start-menu shortcut. Neither build requires Python.
The Windows executable is not code-signed. If you are uncomfortable running a prebuilt beta, the repository includes the source and build instructions.

When reporting a bug, include the game version, map size/seed, factions, difficulty, what happened and what you expected. Add a screenshot, relevant save, or a short excerpt from debug.dat after checking it for personal information.
